subject.title: Cron session accumulation can silently exhaust agent context window — no guardrails or warnings

question: Should this broad cron session accumulation issue remain the umbrella while the retention and cadence guardrail PRs are decided, or should maintainers split it around narrower canonical items now?
rationale: Current main still has a real retention gap, but warning thresholds and schedule limits change operator-facing cron policy and overlap open maintainer-reviewed PRs.

options.title: Keep Umbrella Open
options.body: Keep this issue open until the active retention and cadence guardrail PRs are landed, replaced, or explicitly rejected, then close or split leftover warning work.

options.title: Narrow To Retention
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89666 the canonical retention item and create a separate follow-up for context-pressure warnings or cadence policy.

options.title: Close After Slice Decisions
options.body: Close this issue only after maintainers record the slice decisions and confirm no untracked guardrail behavior remains.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella Open
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until the active retention and cadence guardrail PRs are landed, replaced, or explicitly rejected, then close or split leftover warning work.

likelyOwner.reason: openperf owns the active PR that defines the riskiest cron base-session lifecycle semantics maintainers need to accept or revise.
